How is it that he who came down from the surpassing height that is immaterial and beyond all things, into the virgin's womb, without leaving the Father's womb; who was conceived and took flesh, and of his own will travelled through sufferings to death; who won incorruption for what was corruptible, and went back up to the Father with a body that had its birth from the earth: how is it that he drew his Mother according to the flesh to his own Begetter, lifting her, who had been called an earthly heaven, up to the heavenly land?
title: Homily III — A third hymn for the Mother of God

english: Today the spiritual and living ladder (Genesis 28:12), by which the Most High came down and was seen on earth and lived among men (Baruch 3:37), has used death as a ladder and gone up from earth to heaven. Today the earthly table, which without knowing marriage carried the heavenly bread of life (John 6:35), the coal of the Godhead, has been lifted from earth to heaven; and for the eastern gate of God (Ezekiel 44:1–2) the gates of heaven have been lifted up (Psalm 24:7). Today the living city of God is moved from the earthly Jerusalem to the Jerusalem above (Galatians 4:26). She who bore as her firstborn and only son the firstborn of all creation (Colossians 1:15), the Only-begotten of the Father, now dwells in the church of the firstborn (Hebrews 12:23); and the ark of the Lord, living and endowed with reason, passes over to the rest of her Son (Psalm 132:8). The gates of paradise are opened and receive the field that bore God, from which sprang the tree of eternal life that undid the disobedience of Eve and the death of Adam.

This tree is Christ, the cause of life for all. A hewn cave receives the mountain no hand had quarried, from which a stone cut without hands has filled the whole world (Daniel 2:34–35). The bridal chamber of the divine incarnation of the Word rests in the all-glorious tomb as in a chamber. From there she goes up to the heavenly bridal hall, reigning in full view with her Son and God; and she has left the tomb behind as a bridal chamber for those on earth.

The tomb a bridal chamber? Yes, more splendid than any bridal chamber: not flashing with the gleam of gold, the brightness of silver and the clear sparkle of precious stones, not woven of silken threads, of robes spun with gold and of purple, but with the radiance of the all-holy Spirit, bright with the light of God. It does not bring about the joining of bodies for those who love the earth; for those who are prisoners of the Spirit it brings about the life of holy souls, a state with God better and sweeter than any other.

This tomb is lovelier than Eden. I will not speak of what happened there: the goodwill of the enemy, his kindly advice, if I may call it that, the envy, the deceit, the weakness of Eve, the persuasion, the sweet and bitter bait, through which her mind was stolen and she in turn stole away her husband, the disobedience, the exile, the death. I will not speak of these, so as not to make the feast an occasion of gloom. This tomb raised a mortal body from earth to heaven; Eden brought the father of our race down from on high to earth. For was it not in Eden that he who had been made in the divine image (Genesis 1:27) was condemned with the words, “You are earth, and to earth you shall return” (Genesis 3:19)?

This tomb is more precious than the tabernacle of old (Hebrews 9:2). It has received the living lampstand, endowed with reason and shining with the light of God, and the life-bearing table, which held not the bread of the presence but heavenly bread, and received not material fire but the immaterial fire of the Godhead. This tomb is more blessed than the ark of Moses, for its portion was not shadows and figures but the truth itself. For it received the pure and golden jar that bore the heavenly manna as its fruit (Hebrews 9:4); the living tablet which, by the finger that is the all-powerful Spirit (Exodus 31:18), received the Word of God who was to become flesh, the Word who subsists in his own person; the golden censer, she who conceived the divine coal and filled all creation with fragrance.
title: Homily III — The tomb finer than Eden and the ark

english: Let the demons flee; let the thrice-wretched Nestorians and their leader, the new Pharaoh, the bitter destroyer and tyrant, wail as the Egyptians did long ago. For they have been buried in the depths of their blasphemy (Exodus 15:4–5). But let us who were saved with dry feet (Exodus 14:29) and have crossed the salt sea of ungodliness sing to the Mother of God the song of her exodus.

Let Miriam, the Church, take the timbrel in her hands and lead off the festal song (Exodus 15:20–21). Let the young women of the spiritual Israel go out with timbrels and dances, shouting for joy. Kings of the earth and judges with rulers, young men and virgins, old men with the younger (Psalm 148:11–12): let them sing hymns to the Mother of God. Let assemblies, and words of every kind, and the varied tongues of nations and peoples compose a new song. Let the air resound all around with spiritual reeds and trumpets, and let it fashion a new day of salvation with flashes of fire. Rejoice, you heavens, and let the clouds rain down gladness (Isaiah 45:8). Leap, you rams of God's chosen flock, you divine apostles, raised up like high and lofty mountains by the loftiest contemplations; and you lambs of God, holy people, nurslings of the Church, like hills reaching up by your own choice toward the high mountains (Psalm 114:4).

Ah! Ah! Has the fountain of life died, the Mother of my Lord (Luke 1:43)? Yes, for what was put together from earth had to return to earth (Genesis 3:19), and so pass over to heaven, receiving from the earth, through the laying of her body in it, the gift of a life wholly pure. For like gold she had to cast off the earthy and lustreless thickness of mortality, and, with death as the furnace, to rise from the tomb with her flesh incorrupt and pure, shining with the light of incorruption.
title: Homily III — A new exodus song, and why she had to die

english: Today she receives the beginning of a second existence from him who gave her the beginning of her first existence: she who gave the beginning of a second existence, I mean bodily existence, to him who had no beginning in time of his first and eternal existence, even though he had the Father as his beginning, as the cause of his divine existence.

Rejoice, Zion, holy mountain of God, in which the living mountain of God dwelt; the new Bethel, in which a pillar has been anointed (Genesis 28:18–19), human nature anointed with the Godhead. From you her Son was raised up to the height of heaven, as from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:9–12).

Let a cloud be made ready, as wide as the world and encircling it, and wings of winds to carry the apostles across from the ends of the earth to Zion. Who are these that fly like clouds (Isaiah 60:8) and like eagles to the body (Matthew 24:28) that is the cause of resurrection for all, to serve the Mother of God? Who is this who comes up, all in white (Song of Songs 8:5), all fair (Song of Songs 4:7), shining like the sun (Song of Songs 6:10)? Let the harps of the Spirit sing, the tongues of the apostles. Let the cymbals sound aloud, the foremost of the theologians. Let Hierotheus, the chosen vessel (Acts 9:15), consecrated to the divine Spirit, who in divine union both underwent and learned divine things, go wholly out of the body; let him wholly go forth with her in his will, and beat time to the refrains.

Let all the nations clap their hands (Psalm 47:1); let all sing hymns to the Mother of God. Let angels serve a mortal body. Daughters of Jerusalem, follow after the queen, and as virgins near her, youthful in the Spirit, be brought along with her to the Bridegroom (Psalm 45:14), to stand at the right hand of the Master (Psalm 45:9).

Come down, come down, Master, and as one in her debt repay your Mother what is owed for your nursing. Spread out your divine hands; receive your mother's soul, you who on the cross committed your spirit into your Father's hands (Luke 23:46). Speak to her some sweet whisper: “Come, my fair one, my close one (Song of Songs 2:10), you who shine brighter than the sun with the beauty of virginity. You gave me a share in what is yours; come, enjoy with me what is mine. Come, Mother, to your Son; come, reign with him who, born of you, became poor with you (2 Corinthians 8:9).” Depart, Lady, depart; not as Moses did, “Go up, and die” (Deuteronomy 32:49–50), but rather die, and so go up. Commit your soul into the hands of your Son. Give back to the dust what belongs to the dust, since it will be taken up along with you.

Lift up your eyes, people of God, lift them up. See, the ark of the Lord God of hosts is in Zion, and the apostles stood beside it in the body, burying the body that is the source of life and that received God. Immaterially and invisibly, angels attend it in awe, standing by the Mother of their own Master as servants. The Lord himself is present, he who is present everywhere, fills all things and encompasses the universe, who is in no place; for all things are in him (Colossians 1:17), as in the cause that makes them and holds them together.

See, the Virgin, the daughter of Adam and Mother of God, because of Adam gives her body over to the earth, but because of her Son gives up her soul to the dwellings of heaven. Let the holy city be sanctified, and in addition to its blessings let it reap an eternal blessing. As the divine tabernacle passes, let angels go before it and make the tomb ready. Let the radiance of the Spirit adorn it. Let perfumes be prepared and poured over the all-blameless and all-fragrant body. Let a pure stream be at hand and draw blessing from the undefiled spring of blessing. Let the earth rejoice at the laying down of the body. Let the air leap at the going up of the spirit. Let breezes blow, dewy and full of grace. Let all creation keep festival for the going up of the Mother of God. Let choirs of the young shout for joy. Let the tongues of orators flow with hymns; let the hearts of the wise reflect on the wonder; let the old, whose grey hair is worthy of respect, quietly bring forth the fruit of their contemplation. Let all creation bring its share to the common feast. For not even so would they reach the smallest part of what she deserves.
title: Homily III — All creation escorts her to the tomb

english: Come, let us all go out in spirit with her as she departs. Come, let us all, with the longing of our hearts, go down with her as she goes down to the tomb. Let us stand around the most holy bier. Let us sing holy hymns, chanting something like this: “Rejoice, you who are full of grace; the Lord is with you (Luke 1:28). Rejoice, you who were foreordained to be Mother of God. Rejoice, you who were chosen beforehand in the counsel of God before the ages: most divine shoot of the earth, dwelling-place of divine fire, most holy ornament of the Holy Spirit, spring of living water, paradise of the tree of life, living branch of the divine cluster of grapes that pours out nectar and ambrosia, river full of the fragrances of the Spirit, field of the divine ear of grain, rose most radiant in virginity and breathing out the fragrance of grace, lily of the royal robe, ewe who bore the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29), workshop of our salvation, higher than the angelic powers, servant and mother.”

Come, let us stand around the undefiled tomb and draw divine grace. Come, let us carry the ever-virgin body in the arms of our souls, and go in with her into the tomb, and die with her, dying to the passions of the body, but living with her a life free of passion and undefiled. Let us listen to the divine hymns that come from the immaterial lips of the angels. Let us go in to venerate, and come to know the strangeness of the mystery: how she has been lifted up, how she has been raised on high, how she has been taken up to heaven, how she stands beside her Son above all the ranks of angels. For nothing stands between Mother and Son.

This third discourse on your departure, after the two before it, I have made for you, Mother of God, in reverence and love for the Trinity, whom you served when, by the good pleasure of the Father and the power of the Spirit, you received the Word who has no beginning, the all-powerful wisdom and power of God (1 Corinthians 1:24). Accept, then, my eagerness, which goes beyond my ability, and grant us salvation: freedom from the passions of the soul, relief from the diseases of the body, release from hardships, a peaceful course of life, the illumination of the Spirit. Kindle our longing for your Son; make our life pleasing to him; so that we too, having attained the blessedness of that world and seeing you shining with the glory of your Son, may send up holy hymns, rejoicing for ever in the assembly of those who keep festival in a way worthy of the Spirit, to him who through you built our salvation, Christ, the Son of God and our God. To him be glory and power, with the Father who has no beginning and the all-holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and to all the endless ages of ages. Amen.
title: Homily III — Greeting her at the tomb, and the closing prayer
